verdict: Rollout FAILED: the experiment ran, but val_bpb = 1.013799 did not improve on the current best 1.013711 by more than the required 0.0005 (lower is better).

insights_in_context.hint: Do not extrapolate the successful SSLL change to all-full attention; the mixed-window pattern was the winning point, so keep or refine around SSLL instead.
Changing DEPTH alone also changed the model width in this setup, so you must explicitly hold MODEL_DIM at 512 for a true depth-9 comparison.
An apparent win must be confirmed with one fresh re-run before declaring the experiment successful.
The head-dimension change itself was the mistake: 4 heads of dimension 128 were much better than 8 heads of dimension 64, so HEAD_DIM should have stayed at 128.

insight.hint: Do not spend the one experiment on a tiny interpolation of an already-tuned hyperparameter when the historical evidence is within noise; choose an untried knob with a more plausible chance of beating the threshold.

judge.summary: The agent read the repo and experiment history, then chose a small untested point in the LR warmdown sweep by changing WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.7 to 0.8 in train.py. It committed this one-line change and ran the experiment. The run completed successfully with val_bpb 1.013799 and peak VRAM about 22.6 GB, which is slightly worse than the current best 1.013711 and therefore does not meet the required improvement threshold.
judge.feedback: The decisive problem was not a code bug but a low-value experimental choice: the agent treated a 0.000345 pre-compile near-miss at warmdown 0.9 as evidence that 0.8 might uncover a new optimum, even though that difference was within noise and measured before the current best was achieved by max-autotune compilation. After the compile change, the only post-change comparison is 0.7 (current best) versus 0.8, and a 0.1 shift in an already-tuned linear warmdown fraction is unlikely to produce the required >0.0005 val_bpb improvement. The reasoning should have prioritized an unexplored axis with larger plausible effect, such as weight decay, unembedding LR, Muon momentum, or attention KV heads, rather than interpolating a small local schedule value.
judge.corrected_step: WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1      # cautious weight decay for Muon
